html:
The sinking of USS Housatonic happened on the night of 17 February 1864, just outside Charleston Harbor in South Carolina, United States. The Confederate submarine H. L. Hunley sank the Union warship Housatonic. It was the first time a submarine sank an enemy ship in war. The Hunley and its crew of eight were lost the same night.

In the American Civil War the Union navy blockaded Charleston. The Confederates tried new weapons to break the blockade. The Hunley was an iron tube 12 metres long. Seven men turned a crank to drive its propeller. Its weapon was a charge of gunpowder on a long pole at the bow. It had already sunk twice in trials, killing 13 men. On 17 February it reached the Housatonic some 6 km offshore. The charge blew a hole in the hull, and the ship sank in five minutes. Five of its crew died. Why the Hunley never came back is still argued over.

The blockade went on, and Charleston fell a year later. No submarine sank a warship again until 1914. The wreck was raised in 2000. Like the ironclads at Hampton Roads, it showed how machines would change war at sea.
